body.x: Letitu Corp. (CEO Marco Dahun Lee) will participate in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, to introduce its integrated academic and career roadmap service, “The Pond,” at the “K-Startup Pavilion.” Founded in 2021 to address educational gaps, Letitu draws on its CEO’s 14 years of career counseling experience and established a U.S. branch in Delaware in 2023 to expand globally.

The company leverages AI and data to help schools, teachers, and counselors effectively support students. Letitu empowers educators to guide students in meaningful and precise academic and career planning by simplifying career counseling processes. The company provides personalized learning roadmaps and tailored college recommendations through The Pond, fostering collaboration among students, educators, and institutions with data-driven tools.

Letitu has demonstrated its technical prowess and growth potential by participating in major startup support programs, including TIPS, NEST, and Google’s ChangGoo Program. Building on this success, the company launched The Pond for Students in March 2022, achieving over 10,000 sign-ups within two months. In 2024, it expanded with The Pond for Schools, collaborating with Korean high schools, international schools, and educational institutions in the U.S., Malaysia, and Kazakhstan to penetrate the global B2B market.

The Pond helps students and counselors with university admissions through a comprehensive student management system. The platform creates personalized education roadmaps by analyzing student data, career aspirations, and university requirements. It also offers AI-powered tools for college matching, academic progress tracking, and extracurricular recommendations. Its user-friendly interface and comprehensive dashboard make student management efficient, enabling educators to seamlessly design and execute detailed academic plans.

Letitu is focusing on the rapidly growing Southeast Asian edtech market, targeting international schools in the region. The market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 13.9% from 2024 to 2032, driven by rising demand for digital education, increased government investment, and widespread adoption of smart devices. The number of international schools in Southeast Asia rose from 1,528 in 2017 to 1,905 in 2022, reflecting heightened demand for quality education.

A Letitu representative noted, “This environment is ideal for expanding The Pond. We aim to increase market share in Southeast Asia by forming partnerships with local educational institutions and providing tailored services to meet their specific needs.” The company highlighted that challenges such as diverse educational systems, international curricula, and varying operational priorities necessitate careful customization of its services. The Pond is designed to accommodate international curricula like IB, AP, and A-Level while remaining flexible to school-specific needs.

To address these challenges, Letitu customizes its services to align with individual school requirements, ensuring high compatibility in diverse educational environments. “Our biggest challenge in global expansion is identifying schools that not only need but are ready to use digital solutions like The Pond effectively,” the representative added. “We prioritize fostering long-term partnerships with schools that see value in digital transformation to maximize educational impact.”

Letitu actively participates in key international education and edtech events like the Bett Show and IB Global Conference to connect with potential clients, build brand awareness, and monitor global market trends. Through follow-up meetings with schools introduced at these events, the company aims to secure contracts and establish itself as a trusted long-term partner.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
